preconditions.description: The number of cities n is between 2 and 500, inclusive.
The number of roads m is between 0 and the maximum possible number of roads, which is n * (n - 1) / 2.
Each city number xi and yi is between 1 and n, inclusive.
Each road connects two distinct cities.
Each road length li is between 1 and 10^6, inclusive.

postconditions.description: The output sequence contains (n * (n - 1) / 2) - 1 elements, corresponding to the number of distinct pairs s, t where s < t.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= cst <= m for cst in output)
postconditions.description: Each element cst in the output sequence is between 0 and m, inclusive, representing the number of roads that can lie on the shortest path from s to t.

postconditions.expression: all(output[i] <= output[i + 1] for i in range(len(output) - 1))
postconditions.description: The output sequence is non-decreasing, ensuring that the order of pairs s, t is correct.

postconditions.expression: all(output[i] == 0 if not path_exists(i, i + 1) else True for i in range(len(output) - 1))
postconditions.description: If there is no path between any pair of cities s and t, the corresponding element in the output sequence is 0.

invariants.expression: all(xi != yi for xi, yi, li in roads)
invariants.description: No road connects a city to itself.

invariants.expression: all(1 <= s <= n and 1 <= t <= n for s, t in city_pairs)
invariants.description: All city pairs s, t are valid city numbers.

invariants.expression: all(s < t for s, t in city_pairs)
invariants.description: All city pairs s, t are in the correct order s < t.
